TITLE:
6Li(n,t)alpha angular distribution measurements for
0.2 < En < 10MeV at LANSCE/WNR.
AUTHOR:
(M.Devlin,T.N.Taddeucci,G.M.Hale,R.C.Haight,
J.M.O'Donnell)
FACILITY:
(LINAC,1USALAS)Los Alamos Neutron Science Center/
Weapons Neutron Research (LANSCE/WNR) spallation
neutron source. The WNR neutron source at a 30-degree
production angle provided the continuous-in-energy
source of neutrons.
INC-SOURCE:
(SPALL) Neutron beam was produced by spallation
following the bombardment of a tungsten target by
800 MeV protons at the weapons neutron research
facility (WNR) of the Los Alamos Neutron Science
DETECTOR:
(TELES,PROPC,SIBAR,CSICR) Four three-stage particle
telescopes, which  were variously positioned at eight
scattering angles during the experiment. Each telescope
consisted of a de gas detector (20 torr of p-10 gas,
10% methane in 90% argon), followed by a Si de detector
500 mu-m thick, and finally by a CsI detector. Reaction
products were stopped in Si detector.
METHOD:
(TOF) incident neutron energy was determined using
the time-of-flight technique, corrected for the
time-of-flight of the subsequent reaction product
detected.
(EDE) Used for reaction product identification
MONITOR:
(92-U-235(N,F),,SIG) Fission chamber located
16.32 meters from the source.
ERR-ANALYS:
(ERR-S) Counting statistics including fission chamber.
(ERR-1) Systematic uncertainty for each lab angle
[rms, N-1 weight]: from proton averages: rms = 4.0%
from alpha averages: rms = 5.4% from triton averages:
rms = 5.4% ( <= 60 deg) rms = 6.0% ( 70 - 90 deg) rms
= 10.3% (120 - 135 deg)
(ERR-2,2.,3.) An overall target thickness uncertainty
of a few percent or so - the target was dissolved in
acid and put though mass spect to determine the total
mass, but there are still uncertainties in the beam
and target overlap, as both are not entirely uniform.
STATUS: (APRVD) Approved by Matt Devlin on April 26, 2021.
HISTORY:
(20080117C) Compiled by S.H.
(20100321A) Reference to Koln conference and subs 18 -
21 added, status of subs 2-17 edited.
(20120814U) SD: vol. and page were added to the ref.
of 2007Nice.
(20210422A) BP: Added the final data from authors for
6Li, included data for (n,p) subentries
22-26, corrected order of references,
added doi.

AUTHOR: (Y.ODA, J.SANADA, S.YAMABE)
TITLE:
-ON THE ANGULAR DISTRIBUTION OF 3.1 MEV NEUTRONS
SCATTERED BY PROTONS-
ANALYSIS:
.CROSS-SECTIONS OBTAINED BY SUBTRACTING THE
CONTRIBUTION OF CARBON AND OXYGEN FROM THE CROSS-
SECTIONS OF PARAFFIN AND WATER RESPECTIVELY.
MONITOR:
.THE ASSUMPTION WAS MADE THAT THE IONIZATION
CURRENT IN THE IONIZATION CHAMBER PRODUCED
BY NEUTRONS WHICH LOST THEIR ENERGY THROUGH
THE COLLISION WITH PROTONS, WAS PROPORTIONAL
TO THE PRODUCT OF THE ENERGY AFTER COLLISION
AND THE TOTAL SCATTERING CROSS SECTION OF
NEUTRONS AT THAT ENERGY. THE TOTAL
SCATTERING CROSS  SECTION = 2.224 +- 0.113
BARN WAS USED, C.L.BAILEY ET AL., PHYS. REV.
70(1946)583
FLAG:
(1.) PARAFFIN SAMPLE,  50.7 GRAMS.
(2.) PARAFFIN SAMPLE,  71.8 GRAMS.
(3.) PARAFFIN SAMPLE,  94.9 GRAMS.
(4.) PARAFFIN SAMPLE,  95.4 GRAMS.
(5.) PARAFFIN SAMPLE, 141.4 GRAMS.
(6.) WATER SAMPLE,     94.1 GRAMS.
HISTORY:
(711010C)
(740626E)
(840106U) A.P.T. JAPAN CODE CHANGED TO JPN
(840106E)
ERR-ANALYS:
.ERROR GIVEN MAINLY FROM ERROR  OF THE TOTAL CROSS-
SECTION USED IN THE CALCULATION OF THE SENSITIVITY
OF THE IONIZATION CHAMBER.
.ANGULAR RESOLUTION(C.M.) = +-10 DEGREES.
